quote: just first thing All I wanna know is what's the what's the, you know, general range of cost for something like that.
stewart_read: This is exactly the trigger phrase set for price_estimate_before_design ('give me a ballpark'). The rep's actual response covers similar ground informally but never uses the canonical framing ('totally fair to ask... 30 seconds... real numbers not a random ballpark') that would have named the exchange explicitly and likely short-circuited the four-round argument that follows.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's bill-swap explanation was itself a valid strategy-match redirect, so this could be read as compliant rather than missed.
coaching_implication: Have the rep practice naming the trade explicitly at the first ask ('fair question — here's why I need 30 seconds of info to get you a real number instead of a ballpark') so the customer hears a clear reason instead of open-ended process language.

quote: Alright. Well, I don't understand why you can't just give me a general idea of what what we're talking about rather than wasting a lot of time.
stewart_read: Second touch of the same objection — customer restates it more sharply, calling the process 'wasting a lot of time.' Rep repeats process justification instead of pivoting to the canonical redirect_to_design language.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been intentionally holding scope discipline rather than caving — a defensible read given she never fabricated a number.
coaching_implication: This is the second consecutive round of the same unresolved friction — worth showing the rep the compounding pattern, not just the single instance.

quote: Alright. Well, why can't you just take an average of per month? I I don't know how you how you do it. I mean, you're just giving me a runaround right now.
stewart_read: Third touch — customer now uses the word 'runaround,' a clear trust-erosion signal. Rep responds with more technical justification (on-peak/off-peak, sunlight measurement) rather than acknowledging the frustration or flipping the objection.
alternative_hypothesis: None — by the third round, continuing the same unacknowledged technical justification is a reactive failure to adapt tactics.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly acknowledge frustration ('I hear you, this feels like a runaround') before repeating the process explanation — acknowledgment resets the tone, repetition alone does not.

quote: You're still not answering my question. Just evading everything I want to know about what what's the cost of installation?
stewart_read: Fourth and final touch, now an explicit accusation of evasion. This is the call's lowest trust point and directly precedes the rep finally landing on the working verbal-readback path.
coaching_implication: This moment should be the anchor clip in the 1-on-1 — four rounds of the same objection escalating unchecked to open accusation is the single most replayable failure on this call.

quote: Alright. Well, I can just read it off to you if you, you know, if you wanna see the graph.
stewart_read: The customer handed the rep the exact solution to the photo-collection friction unprompted, and the rep did not take it immediately — she reiterated the photo/text request instead, costing roughly four more minutes before finally accepting verbal read-back at 09:39.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have been holding out for the photo because it's more accurate/complete data for the design team, which is a legitimate operational preference.
coaching_implication: Train reps to accept a customer-offered alternative path immediately when it's offered, especially once resistance has already surfaced once — delaying the pivot compounds the friction that's already visible in the transcript.

quote: No. I'm just trying to figure out exactly what's going on. If there's no if there's no upfront cost, don't pay anything. Then who's who's paying for installing whatever it is?
stewart_read: This is a closer-tier financial mechanism question. The rep answers it fully in real time (net metering explanation, nighttime credit banking, production shortfall risk) rather than using the universal escape hatch, extending a call that was already showing friction.
alternative_hypothesis: Answering briefly may have been necessary to keep the customer from disengaging entirely, given his escalating frustration — a full deflection risked reinforcing the 'runaround' perception.
coaching_implication: Coach on where the line is: a one-line reassurance is fine, but the multi-turn net-metering / production-shortfall explanation at 11:01-12:39 is specialist content that could have been bridged ('great question, that's exactly the kind of thing the specialist maps out for your specific roof') without reigniting the argument.

quote: Last month, the last bill I got was $700.
stewart_read: A strong, dramatic anchor point — $700 in one month — landed early (under 2 minutes) but the rep's response ('Woah. Okay.') stayed sympathetic/neutral rather than flipping it into alignment-against-the-utility.
coaching_implication: See bill_anchor_audit for the flip-execution detail; this is the moment the flip should have happened.
